clue.text: Bead on fastener for nut

parts.note: a screw is a threaded fastener
a bead is a small ball, as in a bead of sweat

explanation.surface: A craft instruction: thread a bead onto a bolt in place of the nut.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' means placed after, so the bead comes second. 'Nut' looks like hardware to go with the fastener, but it is the slang sense of an eccentric person.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal words for a crazy or eccentric person.

clue.text: Empty puzzle, tantalising thing?

parts.note: to empty a room is to strip it
a teaser is a puzzle, as in brain-teaser

explanation.surface: A blank puzzle grid is a tantalising thing for any solver.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful definition: the performer is the one who tantalises.
explanation.definitionFit: A striptease performer tantalises an audience by revealing slowly, so the performer is literally a tantalising person.

clue.text: Celebrate finding upright character in schedule

indicators.note: something placed in a thing sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a roster is a duty schedule
the capital letter I is a single upright stroke

explanation.surface: Someone celebrates on spotting an honest person's name on the work rota.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upright character' suggests a person of integrity; here it is a letter of the alphabet that stands straight.
explanation.definitionFit: To roister is to revel noisily, an old-fashioned word for boisterous partying.

clue.text: Gathering last of rice, I didn't quite get that grain

to gather something in is to enclose it, so one piece surrounds another

parts.note: the reply when you mishear someone

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter, so only the end is kept

parts.note: final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone harvesting rice mishears a remark about the grain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I didn't quite get that' is a whole phrase standing for the single word you say when you mishear: what?
explanation.definitionFit: Wheat is a cereal crop, and its seeds are among the most familiar of all grains.

clue.text: While very cold, I consumed first of daiquiris, mixed

parts.note: as means while, as in 'as I walked'
so means very, as in 'so cold'
C is the abbreviation for cold on a tap
taken as written
consumed food means ate it

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: opening letter of the cocktail

explanation.surface: Someone shivering knocks back the first round of cocktails, all stirred together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mixed' looks like an anagram signal or a cocktail being shaken, but it is the definition, as in mixing with friends.
explanation.definitionFit: To have mixed with people is to have associated with them; both verbs mean keeping company socially.

clue.text: Record claiming a steering mechanism is doing little

indicators.note: to claim something is to take hold of it, so one piece holds another

parts.note: a log is a written record, as in a ship's log
taken as written
a fin steers a fish, or keeps a boat or aircraft on course

explanation.surface: A record-keeping system that takes over the steering leaves the pilot with nothing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: The record splits around the article and the fin.
explanation.definitionFit: Loafing means idling about or lazing, spending time with no effort or useful activity.

clue.text: Ride wave ahead of ship

parts.note: a roller is a long heavy wave
a coaster is a ship that trades along the coast

explanation.surface: A surfer rides a wave just in front of a ship's bow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ride' reads as a verb for surfing the wave, but it is a noun: a fairground ride.
explanation.definitionFit: A rollercoaster is a fairground or theme-park ride on a steep, twisting track.

clue.text: Those perhaps working for a hotel inspector, ties knotted

definitions.text: Those perhaps working for a hotel

indicators.note: knotted string is twisted and tangled, so these letters are tangled into a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Hotel staff greet a visiting inspector, nervously knotting their ties.
explanation.walkthrough: The hotel inspector seems the subject, but the inspector is merely letters; 'perhaps' marks the definition as an example, since receptionists work in many places.
explanation.definitionFit: Hotel front-desk staff who greet guests and handle bookings are typical examples of this job.

clue.text: Dog possesses article, and licks around it with love

indicators.note: to go around something is to encircle it, so one piece wraps another

parts.note: a cat laps or licks up milk
to possess is to have
the indefinite article
love is zero in tennis scoring, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A dog owns something and licks all around it lovingly.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'it' after 'around' points back to the possessing and the article, which go inside the licking. The love comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lhasa apso is a small long-haired breed originally from Tibet, named after its capital city.

clue.text: Welcome them briefly, a couple

indicators.note: to say something briefly is to clip it short, so letters are dropped

parts.note: the informal 'em with the first two letters dropped
a brace is a pair, as in a brace of pheasants

explanation.surface: A host greets a pair of guests with a quick hello.
explanation.walkthrough: A couple suggests two lovers, but it is just the number two, as hunters say of game birds.
explanation.definitionFit: To embrace an idea is to welcome it gladly, and an embrace is also a hug of greeting.

clue.text: Never interact, only when circulating

indicators.note: things circulating move about the room, so these letters move around into a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Party advice: never get chatting with anyone, except while moving round the room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Never' is used as an emphatic refusal, as in 'Never!' when asked to do something.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are emphatic spoken refusals, the exclamation a person gives to reject a suggestion outright.

clue.text: A naval officer says they're infidels

parts.note: taken as written
PO is a petty officer in the navy
to state something is to say it

explanation.surface: A sailor in charge declares that certain people are unbelievers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Says' looks like a sound-alike signal, but it simply supplies a synonym. PO is the standard abbreviation for petty officer.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostate has abandoned their religious faith, which makes them a kind of unbeliever in the eyes of former fellow worshippers.

clue.text: Bags of Scottish tenacity rarely evident with Scots first of all

indicators.note: the first of every word means taking each opening letter in turn

parts.note: opening letters of these five words

explanation.surface: Scottish dogged determination is seldom seen, even among Scots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bags' is old slang for trousers, so 'Bags of Scottish' means Scottish trousers rather than a great deal of Scottishness.
explanation.definitionFit: Trews are close-fitting tartan trousers traditionally worn in Scotland, and bags is dated British slang for loose trousers.

clue.text: Person clearing the way, announcing emotional islander?

indicators.note: announcing is speaking out loud, so we want what the words sound like

parts.note: a weeper is an emotional person, and this one comes from the Greek island of Rhodes

explanation.surface: A tearful islander comes forward, making way for a procession.
explanation.walkthrough: Rhodes is a Greek island; someone from there who cries is a 'Rhodes weeper', which said out loud matches the street cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: A road sweeper cleans streets, literally clearing the way of litter and leaves for traffic and pedestrians.

clue.text: Lift maintained by bra is extraordinary

indicators.note: something maintained by others is held up within them, so the letters sit inside these words

parts.note: the letters run across these three words

explanation.surface: An advert boasting that a bra gives remarkable uplift.
explanation.walkthrough: The underwear surface makes 'Lift' look like support; it is just a verb meaning to raise.
explanation.definitionFit: To lift something and to raise it both mean moving it to a higher position.

clue.text: Formality, warning for drivers in court once

parts.note: starch is stiffness of manner, as in a starchy person
the amber traffic light warns drivers to stop

explanation.surface: Motorists in a courtroom of the past receive a formal caution.
explanation.walkthrough: In the UK the amber light comes between green and red and warns drivers that the signal is about to change.
explanation.definitionFit: The Star Chamber was an English court of the Tudor and Stuart era, abolished in 1641 and notorious for arbitrary judgements.

clue.text: Piano parts over before a dramatic work

indicators.note: to part something is to split it open, so one piece pushes into the middle of another

parts.note: o'er is the poetic contraction of over
p is the musical marking for piano, meaning softly
taken as written

explanation.surface: Instrumental piano sections finish before the staging of a theatrical piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parts' reads as a plural noun for musical sections, but it is a verb: the soft marking splits the poetic 'o'er'.
explanation.definitionFit: An opera is a staged work in which a drama is set to music and sung.

clue.text: Crunchy food in vessel served with puree of apricots

parts.note: a pot is a cooking vessel

indicators.note: a puree mashes fruit into pulp, so these letters are mashed into a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A dish of something crunchy served up with fruit puree.
explanation.walkthrough: A potato crisp is the British name for what Americans call a potato chip: a thin fried slice sold in packets.
explanation.definitionFit: Crisps are thin fried slices of potato, prized for their brittle snap when bitten.

clue.text: Protestants against stealing a bread roll, saints

indicators.note: a thief takes goods into their keeping, so one piece holds another

parts.note: anti means against
taken as written
a bap is a soft round bread roll in Britain
St is the abbreviation for saint, so two of them

explanation.surface: Reformers objecting to bread theft by a group of saints.
explanation.walkthrough: The bread roll and the church setting suggest communion wafers. A bap is a soft round bread roll, a word common in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Anabaptists were radical Reformation Protestants who rejected infant baptism and insisted on rebaptising believing adults.

clue.text: Having lost land, Ireland and USA sacked a massive continent

indicators.note: a sacked city is looted and wrecked, so these letters are thrown into disorder
what has been lost is no longer there, so those letters are taken out

parts.note: taken as written, before the loss
these four letters are the ones lost from the country's name
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: After losing territory, Ireland and America ransack an enormous landmass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Land' looks like real territory being lost, but it is just four letters struck out of the country's name. Only what remains plus the USA is rearranged; the final A stays put.
explanation.definitionFit: Eurasia is the single combined landmass of Europe and Asia, the largest continental area on Earth.

clue.text: Second constant, not first, relating to a bone

indicators.note: without its first means the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: s is the abbreviation for second
eternal, meaning constant, with its opening letter dropped

explanation.surface: A fact about the anatomy of the second of two unchanging things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constant' as an adjective means eternal, which loses its E here.
explanation.definitionFit: Sternal is the adjective for the sternum, the flat breastbone joining the ribs at the front of the chest.

clue.text: See good, soft, skin on sausage

parts.note: g is the abbreviation for good
limp means soft and floppy

indicators.note: the skin is the outer layer, so only the outside letters are kept

parts.note: first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A butcher points out a good sausage with soft skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' opens the clue as an instruction, but it is the definition, a verb meaning to catch sight of.
explanation.definitionFit: To glimpse is to see something briefly or partially, catching only a fleeting view of it.

clue.text: Personage listless then?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a person of distinction
second meaning, playful: lacking a list, where the list is a table, read as two words

explanation.walkthrough: 'Listless' normally means lacking energy; read literally it means lacking a list, and a table is a kind of list, so the answer splits as no table. The question mark flags that.
explanation.definitionFit: A notable is a person of importance or distinction, a dignitary; the adjective used as a noun.

clue.text: Makeshift construction short in diameter, joiner crossing the drink

cola is a soft drink

explanation.walkthrough: 'The drink' is crossword slang for the sea or water, which suits a bridge; here it is a soft drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Bricolage is construction improvised from whatever materials are to hand, a term borrowed from French.

clue.text: One of Jerome Kern's smouldering looks after this?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one of the songs of the Broadway composer
second meaning, playful: what makes eyes water and look smouldering, sitting near a fire

explanation.walkthrough: Smouldering looks normally means a sultry gaze; the setter suggests watery eyes after sitting by something smoking. The question mark flags that whimsical second meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a famous Jerome Kern ballad from the 1933 musical Roberta, later a hit for the Platters.

clue.text: Buy from another company, being courteous to engineer?

indicators.note: to engineer something is to rebuild it, so these letters are rebuilt in another order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A firm buys in services elsewhere because it is polite to its engineer.
explanation.walkthrough: The engineer looks like a person; 'to engineer' is a verb telling you to rebuild the letters before it.
explanation.definitionFit: To outsource is to contract work or supplies out to an external firm rather than doing it in-house.

clue.text: What angel has, foxy dresses with some style

explanation.walkthrough: 'Foxy' suggests attractive, but it is the cunning sense; 'dresses' looks like clothing and is the wrapping instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressing sharply means dressing smartly and stylishly, in neat, well-cut clothes.

clue.text: Stop repeating phrase

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as an instruction to stop saying the same thing; the two parts are separate meanings, one a verb and one a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To refrain is to abstain or hold back, and a refrain is a recurring line or chorus in verse.

clue.text: Puck is merely prodded initially

clue.text: Cloth wrapping metal, rank

clue.text: Shrivelled up thing is in shower

explanation.definitionFit: A raisin is a dried grape, its skin wrinkled and shrunken as the water evaporates.

clue.text: Item on executive's desk with a knock-on effect?

clue.text: Using tongue it is turned over, passing flavour around

clue.text: Match where both sides may play away?

clue.text: What I said when I pootled off with minimum of pretence?

clue.text: Warmer for pig's ears? I'm not interested

clue.text: One location for a start, with beach all round?

clue.text: Second note put in score, tremulous

clue.text: Why should I tell you the name of a plant?

clue.text: Bones at times are almost breaking

clue.text: Hose perhaps submerged in river?

clue.text: Recalled pictures perhaps with fungi in ranges of colours

clue.text: US president is very keen on hugs

clue.text: North African upland so described?

clue.text: Most ill at ease, I'd see outline of ghost that's shapeshifting

clue.text: Time when house connects district to old city

clue.text: Repeating a little, our dodgy dish

clue.text: Release pressure in loveless marriage

explanation.surface: Relief from strain within an unhappy marriage.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is zero in tennis, so a loveless word loses its O.
explanation.definitionFit: To unpin something is to release it by removing the pins that hold it fastened.

clue.text: Prophet respected, no way ending in gutter

indicators.note: no means without, so the following letters are taken away

parts.note: august means respected and dignified
st, street, is a way, and these letters go

indicators.note: the ending is the last part, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A venerated seer is denied his path and ends up in the gutter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Way' is a road, abbreviated ST as in street, which comes off the end of the adjective before the R is added.
explanation.definitionFit: An augur was a Roman religious official who foretold events from omens, so a seer.

clue.text: Commotion about one drink Buddhist gets cheap

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes around another

parts.note: ado is fuss or commotion
the Roman numeral for one
mead is a drink made from honey
Zen is a school of Buddhism

explanation.surface: A fuss breaks out over a Buddhist getting a bargain drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buddhist' stands for the school rather than a person. The definition is the phrase's idiomatic sense, so cheap means plentiful and of little value.
explanation.definitionFit: Something a dime a dozen is so common that it is worth very little, an American idiom.

clue.text: Zoroastrian in capital city turning tail

indicators.note: to turn the tail is to swing the end around, so the final letters go the other way

parts.note: Paris is the French capital

explanation.surface: A Zoroastrian in a capital city runs away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning tail' means fleeing in the surface; here only the tail end of the city name turns round, its last two letters swapping.
explanation.definitionFit: The Parsis are Zoroastrians descended from Persians who settled in India, mainly around Mumbai.

clue.text: Be a pig — while a stallion?

definitions.meaning: second meaning, literal: how a male equine takes its meals

explanation.walkthrough: The animals seem to clash; the idiom applies literally to a stallion, which can only eat as its species does. The question mark flags the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to eat greedily in large amounts, which is what being a pig at table means.

clue.text: By inference, maybe honest trial without dispute

parts.note: an honest deal involves no con, or swindle; 'maybe' marks this as an inference
a trial is a test

explanation.surface: A legal opinion that a fair hearing would be undisputed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Honest' is not a synonym here but something to infer from: what is honest has no con in it, which the opening words admit.
explanation.definitionFit: No contest describes an outcome so certain that nobody can challenge it, a one-sided affair.
